_comment: The cross-process advisory lock guarding config.yaml.
Why it exists: config.yaml has two writers — the desktop's configService (in
process, for the Settings pane) and the Go brain (for config.save over the
bus, which is what the web and mobile Settings panes use). Both do the same
three steps:
refresh-if-changed-on-disk  ->  deepMerge(current, partial)  ->  atomic write
The mtime gate each of them has closes only the FIRST step. Nothing spans the
three, so: A refreshes at mtime T0, B refreshes+merges+writes T1, then A merges
its partial onto the stale T0 snapshot and renames over B. B's setting is gone,
silently, and both processes report success.
Why a lock rather than a single owner: neither process is always present.
Headless `workspacer serve` runs with no Electron at all, and the brain is
explicitly optional (the hub logs a warning and serves brain-less when no
binary is found). Section-level ownership does not split them either — the
desktop Settings pane and the web Settings pane write the same keys. The one
section with a real owner, `updates`, is already carved out as host-trusted.
MECHANISM: create `<config.yaml>.lock` with O_EXCL. Holding it spans all three
steps. Release in a finally/defer so a panic cannot wedge it.
staleMs MUST match across implementations. If one side calls a lock stale
sooner than the other, it will steal a lock the other still believes it holds,
which is worse than having no lock at all — both would then write believing
they were exclusive. The filename must match for the obvious reason.
maxWaitMs is deliberately NOT shared. The desktop's saveConfig is synchronous
on the Electron main thread, so its budget is small enough that a pathological
wait cannot be seen as a freeze; the brain is a background process and can
afford to wait longer. Mutual exclusion holds regardless of how long each side
is willing to wait — only the stale threshold is a correctness parameter.
